items.title: CJI Surya Kant to attend NLSIU convocation on October 17
items.summary: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant will attend the 34th convocation of National Law School of India University (NLSIU) on October 17. The University's Executive Council and General Council approved the new date on Wednesday following weeks of uncertainty over whether the ceremony, originally scheduled for September 12, would be held at all. The convocation was cancelled in August after graduating students rejected a demand to issue a public statement inviting the CJI to the ceremony. It later emerged that the demand came days after students had already agreed to a convocation with the CJI present. More than 700 current and former NLSIU students had objected to the CJI and Bar Council of India (BCI) Chairman Manan Kumar Mishra attending the ceremony. The objection followed the BCI's August 13 decisions to halt and, within hours, restore enrolment for NALSAR Hyderabad's graduating batch over its own objection to CJI Kant's presence at its convocation. NLSIU later cancelled the convocation before deciding that it will hold the same with the CJI being present. Students have the option to obtain their degrees at the convocation or in-absentia.

The death toll continues to rise even as hope flickers when we read dramatic stories of people found alive after many days. items.title: NCLT President has power to transfer cases across benches: NCLAT
items.summary: The National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) on Wednesday held that the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) president has powers to transfer cases across benches in various territorial jurisdictions [Kamalesh v. However, proceedings under Section 95 of the IBC against Singla were initiated before NCLT in New Delhi. Singla sought transfer of the personal guarantor proceedings to Chandigarh. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday questioned the basis on which the Annual Performance Appraisal Report (APAR) of Rajasthan judicial officer Rakesh Goyal was downgraded despite favourable assessment by the judges who had directly supervised him. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was hearing an appeal by the Rajasthan High Court's administrative side against a May 2026 judgment of the High Court which had expunged adverse remarks in Goyal’s APAR for 2010. items.title: Objectionable: Delhi High Court on legal resource portals changing para numbers of judgments
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Wednesday frowned upon the practice of legal resource websites like Manupatra and SCC Online changing paragraphs numbers and other grammatical aspects of court judgments. A Division Bench of Justices C Hari Shankar and Vinod Kumar said that changes to the original order copy could distort what the Court wants to convey. “You cannot change the para numbers given by court. Manupatra and SCC Online liberally give their own para numbers. I find it objectionable. Sometimes the way you punctuate or the way you break up a para may convey the impression that the court wants to convey. We find that SCC Online has a different para numbering, Manupatra has a different para numbering, the original para number is completely different," Justice Shankar stated. Justice C Hari Shankar and Justice Vinod Kumar The Court made the remarks while hearing the arguments by online legal database Indian Kanoon in its appeal against a May 29 single-judge ruling. items.title: Offerings made to hereditary temple priest are his personal income, not joint family wealth: Karnataka HC
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently held that offerings made to hereditary temple priests form part of their personal income and not joint family wealth, meaning that property bought using such income would also be personal assets and not joint family property [ Rajamati v Leelavathi ]. A Bench Justices R Nataraj and Tyagaraja N Inavally made the observation while dealing with a family dispute over property purchased using the earnings of a deceased Hindu priest. "If such person, in deference to the traditions in the family, endows himself in the service of the deity and devotees show obeisance to him by offering cash or in kind, then such offerings would be in recognition of the man's service and hence, should be construed as his individual income," the Court said. The Court, however, also clarified that not all offerings made by devotees at a temple accrue to the priest personally. It held that where a trust has been constituted to administer the temple, offerings made by devotees to the temple go into the trust's accounts and cannot be treated as the priest's personal income. items.summary: The Supreme Court will commence hearing the batch of petitions seeking criminalisation of marital rape from next month. Currently, marital rape is excluded from the ambit of the offence of "rape" by way of Exception 2 to Section 375 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC). A similar provision is also present in the newly enacted Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which replaced the IPC in 2023. A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana on Wednesday directed that the matter be listed for final hearing after three weeks on Wednesdays and Thursdays. items.title: Times Now draws ire for recreating Manipur musician’s murder using AI, as family mourns
items.summary: On September 8, a Times Now show titled “Decoding Now”, which airs just before the primetime slot, ran a segment on Chongtham Vikram Singh, a 55-year-old Manipuri musician who was beaten to death outside his South Delhi home late on Sunday night. To illustrate what happened, the channel used a sequence of AI-generated clips. The clips included an AI-generated version of Singh confronting a group of youths outside his apartment; the youths chasing him; the mob assaulting him; and a bloodied man being carried down a staircase. It was captioned “Fists & Blows Rained on Vikram”. Other clips showed a bloodied victim lying in front of his apartment door, being carried down the stairs in a blood-stained T-shirt by a character who is presumably a family member, and then carried into an ambulance. All these clips ran under banners like “Delhi Hangs Its Head In Shame”, “Manipuri Musician Murdered” and “What Killed: Racism or Rage?” as anchor Meghna Deka and panellists Ponting Thokchom of the North East Students’ Society and journalist Subir Bhaumik discussed the tragedy.
